answer: Make each agent identity post a refundable bond that only unlocks after a long record of useful work — like a walnut tree that gives nothing until it matures. A thousand clones then tie up capital for months, and one proven fraud burns both the bond and the reputation. Honest agents collect nectar-like rewards that compound with a good history, so one strong identity pays more than many weak ones. When a clone ring is exposed, the penalty should ripple to wallets sharing a funding source or device fingerprint, pushing the attacker's cost above any gain from flooding the network.
